cleanIntro: The FPC strips through its stock: the stock comes off the receiver tube against buffer-spring pressure, a cross pin releases the recoil spring, and only then do the bolt and charging slide come out. Nothing about it resembles a conventional carbine, so follow the order exactly.

steps.title: Fire only the cartridge marked on the firearm, and nothing marked +P+
steps.action: Check what your FPC is marked for and fire only that unless this manual specifies otherwise. Never use ammunition marked +P+ in it. Note the caliber marking and the serial number on your FPC while you are checking; Smith & Wesson asks owners to record the serial number before shipping a firearm in for service.
steps.prose: The FPC is built in more than one chambering on the same folding platform, which is exactly the situation where a box of the wrong thing gets picked up off a bench. The +P+ objection is that the marking names no defined pressure limit at all — it is a loader's own designation, so two boxes wearing it can be a long way apart in what they generate.
steps.caution: "Plus-P-Plus" (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.quote: WARNING: NEVER USE CARTRIDGES OTHER THAN THOSE DESIGNATED BY THE MARKING ON THE FIREARM UNLESS SPECIFIED IN THIS MANUAL. DOING SO MAY CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH TO THE SHOOTER OR BYSTANDERS AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTY.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Ammunition, WARNING, p.10

steps.title: Muzzle threads differ by caliber — check before fitting anything
steps.action: If you are cleaning the muzzle threads or refitting a thread protector or muzzle device, know your thread pitch: a 9mm FPC has 1/2-28 muzzle threads, while 10mm Auto and 40 S&W have 9/16-24.
steps.prose: Two pitches on one product line and a thread protector that will start on the wrong one is how muzzle threads get destroyed — cross-threading a 1/2-28 device onto a 9/16-24 barrel ruins the barrel, not the device. Read the caliber marking rather than trusting what was in the box with the rifle.
steps.quote:
9mm has 1/2-28 muzzle threads
10mm Auto and 40 S&W have 9/16-24 muzzle threads
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Model & Features Identification, FIGURE 3, p.12

steps.title: Magazine out, safety to SAFE
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Press the magazine catch and take the magazine out, then push the manual safety button to the SAFE position.
steps.prose: Magazine first and then the safety, so nothing can feed while you are working the action a moment later. Remember the FPC carries spare magazines inside the stock as well — those come out separately and are easy to forget when the rifle is 'unloaded'.
steps.quote: Point the muzzle in a safe direction. Make sure your finger is off the trigger and out of the trigger guard. Depress the magazine catch and remove the magazine (FIGURE 46).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.27

steps.title: Charging slide fully back, then closed on an empty chamber
steps.action: Holding the firearm upright with the muzzle in a safe direction, grasp the charging slide and draw it briskly fully rearward to extract anything in the chamber. Then let the bolt close by returning the charging slide fully forward. Take any magazines out of the in-stock storage cavities as well.
steps.prose: The bolt has to end up closed for the strip, which is the opposite of most carbines and means this is the last clear look you get into the chamber — take it before the slide goes forward. The in-stock magazine storage is the FPC's own trap: a rifle with an empty magazine well can still be carrying two loaded magazines in the buttstock.
steps.quote: Allow the bolt to close by returning the charging slide fully forward - so the bolt is in the closed position (FIGURE 49).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.28

steps.title: Use the magazine that came with this FPC
steps.action: Keep your rifle's own magazines with it. Smith & Wesson supplies magazines designed for your specific model and caliber of FPC, and while one may insert into another firearm it will function properly only in the models it was designed for.
steps.prose: The FPC takes M&P pistol magazines by design, so the magazine drawer next to it is full of things that fit and are not right — different caliber, different capacity, different follower. On this rifle a wrong magazine also has to clear the in-stock storage cavities, so it can be wrong in a second way.
steps.quote: Smith & Wesson® has provided you with magazine(s) designed to operate in your specific model and caliber of FPC®.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Loading the M&P FPC, p.19

steps.title: Stock down against the latch, then off the receiver tube
steps.action: Place the butt stock against a stable surface and press down firmly to relieve the tension on the latch. Holding that downward pressure, pull the stock retainer latch out; the receiver tube will move upward against spring pressure as the latch disengages. Then pull the stock, with its internal buffer spring, off the receiver tube.
steps.prose: The buffer spring is what is holding that latch loaded, so pressing down first is not optional — pulling the latch without relieving it means the stock leaves under spring load. The buffer spring usually stays in the stock recess rather than falling out, and if it does come free it can go back into the stock either way round.
steps.quote: While holding downward pressure on the stock, pull the stock retainer latch out and allow the receiver tube to move upward (against spring pressure) when the stock latch disengages from the receiver tube.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.28
steps.warn: You must control the bolt and the recoil spring during removal to keep them from flying out and causing injury.

steps.title: End plug pressed down, cross pin out
steps.action: With the stock off, you can see the recoil spring end plug and the cross pin. Press down firmly on the end plug — about an eighth of an inch — and hold it there while you push the cross pin out of the tube.
steps.prose: The pin is what the whole recoil spring is bearing on, so it will not move until the plug takes the load off it; forcing the pin against spring pressure is what mushrooms it. The pin can go out either direction. Note which end plug you have: some FPC models use a reversible plug and some a buffered directional one, and they go back differently.
steps.quote: Next, press down firmly (about 1/8˝ ) on the spring end plug and hold it there, while you push the cross pin out of the tube (FIGURE 55).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.29

steps.title: Control the recoil spring as it comes up out of the tube
steps.action: Once the cross pin is out the recoil spring pushes upward hard. Control it, then take the spring and end plug out of the tube.
steps.prose: This is the moment the FPC bites: the spring has been compressed against that cross pin the whole time and there is nothing else holding it. Keep a hand over the top of the tube as the pin leaves rather than watching the pin.
steps.quote: Once the cross pin is out - the recoil spring exerts significant pressure upward. Control the spring as it pushes upward (FIGURE 56).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.30
steps.warn: Once the cross pin is out, the recoil spring exerts significant pressure upward.

steps.title: Charging slide lug pin out at the wide spot
steps.action: Draw the charging slide fully rearward until it stops and the bolt carrier shows, then push the charging slide fully forward to reveal the charging slide lug pin. Move the bolt carrier slightly to line the pin up with the wide spot in the receiver tube, turn the receiver so the pin faces down and let it fall out — or push it out through the hole in the top of the tube with a small drift or the lanyard tool.
steps.prose: Alignment with the wide spot is everything: the pin cannot pass the tube wall anywhere else, and prodding at a misaligned pin only peens its end. Gravity does most of the work if you point the pin downward, which is why the manual suggests that before it suggests a tool.
steps.quote: Generally, to get the charging slide lug pin out, simply orient the receiver with the pin facing down and let the pin fall out.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, NOTE, p.31

steps.title: Bolt carrier and bolt out of the tube — control the bolt
steps.action: Pull the bolt carrier and bolt out of the rear of the tube, controlling the bolt as it comes: it is a slip fit on the carrier and will separate from it as it clears the end of the receiver tube.
steps.prose: Nothing holds the bolt to the carrier but the tube, so the moment the assembly clears the end the bolt is a loose part in mid-air. Have a hand under it. That slip fit is also why it goes back together easily once the two are lined up.
steps.quote: The bolt is a slip fit on the bolt carrier and will slide off as the parts exit the receiver tube.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, FIGURE 64, p.32

steps.title: Charging slide off the receiver tube
steps.action: Draw the charging slide rearward, move it about a sixteenth of an inch forward from its rearmost position, and lift it up and off the receiver tube.
steps.prose: That tiny forward movement lines the slide's lug up with the relief in the tube — dead at the rear it will not lift, and forcing it bends the slide. Note which charging slide you have: Type-One and Type-Two are not interchangeable, and a Type-Two is a factory-assembled unit that must not be taken apart.
steps.caution: The Type-One and Type-Two charging handles are not interchangeable, and the Type-Two charging slide assembly must not be taken apart.
steps.quote: Move the charging slide about 1/16˝ forward (from rear-most position) and lift it up and off the receiver tube (FIGURE 67).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, p.32

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Stock with its buffer spring, receiver tube and barrel, bolt, bolt carrier, charging slide, recoil spring with end plug and cross pin, and the magazines — the FPC is now field-stripped for cleaning, and no further disassembly is required to clean it. Never dry-fire the FPC while it is disassembled. Deep Clean covers the magazine, which the manual documents on its own.
steps.prose: The manual's own caption on the field-stripped photograph reads that no further disassembly is required to clean, which is the whole answer to how far to go on this rifle.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is required to clean
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Disassembly/Field Stripping, FIGURE 68 caption, p.32

deepSteps.title: Floor plate catch depressed through the floor plate
deepSteps.action: With the magazine out and empty, use a small tool such as a punch or drift through the hole in the floor plate to depress the floor plate catch.
deepSteps.prose: Match the tool to the hole — too fat and it never reaches the catch, too sharp and it scores the tube where the follower runs. Keep the magazine pointed away from your face from here on, because the catch is riding a compressed spring.
deepSteps.quote: Use a small tool (like a punch or drift) to depress floor plate catch through the hole in the floor plate (FIGURE 93).
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Magazines, Standard Magazine Disassembly, p.40
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the spring and follower so that they do not fly out and cause injury.

deepSteps.title: Floor plate forward, slowly, spring controlled
deepSteps.action: While holding the floor plate catch down against spring pressure, slide the floor plate slowly forward off the tube, controlling the spring movement as you go.
deepSteps.prose: Slowly is the instruction and it earns its place: your thumb has to take over from the punch as the plate travels, and the instant the plate stops covering the catch the spring is pushing it out. On the extended magazine the spring is longer still and holds more.
deepSteps.quote: While holding floor plate catch down against spring pressure (FIGURE 94), slowly slide the floor plate forward off of the tube, being careful to control the spring movement.
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Magazines, Standard Magazine Disassembly, p.40

deepSteps.title: Catch, spring and follower out of the bottom
deepSteps.action: Take the floor plate catch, the spring and the attached follower out through the bottom of the magazine tube, and note their orientation before you set them down.
deepSteps.prose: On the standard FPC magazine the follower is attached to the spring and comes out with it; on the extended magazine it is not attached and the spring is narrower and slanted at the top, so which magazine you are holding changes what you should expect to fall out. Clean the inside of the tube while it is open — that is where residue slows a follower.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the floor plate catch, the spring and the attached follower out through bottom of the magazine tube.
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual For
M&P® FPC® — REV:M&P_FPC-013025 — Magazines, Standard Magazine Disassembly, p.40

cleaning.name: BORE, CHAMBER AND MUZZLE
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish with a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore to remove residue and solvent
Clean the feed ramp and the chamber mouth
Clean the muzzle threads and the thread protector, and refit only a device of the correct pitch for your caliber

cleaning.name: BOLT, CARRIER AND RECEIVER TUBE
tasks: Clean the bolt face, the extractor and the firing pin recess
Clean the bolt carrier and the inside of the receiver tube, which is where a blowback action deposits most of its fouling
Clean the charging slide and the surfaces of the tube it rides on
Clean the charging slide lug pin and the cross pin, and check neither is peened

cleaning.name: STOCK, HINGE AND MAGAZINE
tasks: Clean the buffer spring and the stock recess it sits in
Clean the in-stock magazine storage cavities and the folding hinge and latch
Wipe the magazine tube and feed lips; if it has been apart, clean inside the tube and the follower
Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth and remove all solution, oil and fingerprints

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Lightly coat metal parts inside and out with a high quality firearm oil and wipe the excess away
Do not over-lubricate: excess collects unburned powder and carbon residue and interferes with proper functioning
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this firearm

reassembly: Slide the charging slide back onto the receiver tube at the rear and move it into its running position.
Set the bolt on the bolt carrier and feed the pair into the rear of the tube, then align the charging slide lug with the wide spot and insert the charging slide lug pin.

Drop the recoil spring into the tube, fit the end plug the right way round for your model — reversible or buffered/directional — press it down about an eighth of an inch and push the cross pin back through.
Slide the stock, with its buffer spring in the recess, back onto the receiver tube and press down until the stock retainer latch snaps home.

Magazine: follower, spring and floor plate catch back into the tube in the orientation they came out — the extended magazine's spring is narrower and slanted at the top — then the floor plate slid on until the catch locks it.
Confirm the stock latch is fully engaged before handling the rifle by the stock.
fncheck: With the firearm empty and pointed in a safe direction, confirm the stock retainer latch is fully engaged and that the cross pin is seated flush in the receiver tube. Cycle the charging slide several times and check the bolt runs fully into battery and the bolt catch holds it open on an empty magazine and releases cleanly. Check the manual safety moves positively into SAFE and back. Fold and unfold the rifle and confirm the folding latch locks solidly, then seat an empty magazine and confirm it latches and drops free.
